title: Redwood POC scoping with Orchard Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a 4-week pilot: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs, and benchmark plan (latency/cost/accuracy). Agreement on next steps to share security docs, benchmark scripts, sample dataset and schedule technical deep dive.
topics: SSO / SAML setup and IdP options
Pilot scope: workload sizing, benchmarks, success criteria
next_steps: Maya to send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts + security datasheet
Jonas to share benchmark scripts, infra checklist, and sample prompt set
Karen to provide sample dataset and PII redaction requirements
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) week of Jan 17
Kickoff pilot once security review and infra checklist completed
action_items: Maya Patel: send SOC 2 + ISO artifacts and security datasheet by 2027-01-12
Jonas Chen: share benchmark scripts, infra checklist, and sample prompt set by 2027-01-14
Karen Brooks: provide redacted sample dataset and PII checklist by 2027-01-13
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jonas Chen (Redwood); Karen Brooks, Dr. Samir Patel, Lindsay Park (Orchard Health)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE for your account, and with me is Jonas Chen, our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:07] Karen Brooks: Good, thanks. Busy week but glad we could get this on the calendar.
[00:10] Dr. Samir Patel: Thanks, Maya. We want to focus on the security constraints for the pilot and make sure benchmarks and success criteria are clear.
[00:16] Maya Patel: Absolutely. Our goal today is to scope a pilot that's security-first - SOC 2/ISO appetite, SSO integration, RBAC, audit logging, and then the benchmark plan: latency, throughput, cost, and quality metrics.
[00:28] Jonas Chen: I'll drive the technical bits - sample infra, what we need for a private pilot or dedicated capacity, and the scripts we'll run. Quick ask: what environment are you planning to host sample data in? VPC? On-prem?
[00:38] Lindsay Park: We prefer a VPC peering approach initially. We can consider an on-prem bundle later but for pilot we want Redwood Private via our AWS VPC.
[00:46] Karen Brooks: Important for us: do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scopes we can review? Also SSO via SAML with our Okta instance, RBAC so only certain roles can call the API, and audit logs routed to our SIEM.
[00:58] Maya Patel: Yes - we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts. I'll share the attestation and the scope documents after the call. We support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or pushed to CloudWatch/CloudTrail. We'll include KMS integration for customer-managed keys in Private deployments.
[01:15] Dr. Samir Patel: For RBAC, we need separation between data scientists (read+annotate) and ops (deploy/run). Also want API key rotation policies and admin audit trail.
[01:24] Jonas Chen: On our RBAC model, we have roles you can map to SAML attributes - admin, developer, reader - and every action is logged. For key rotation in Private, you can attach your KMS/HSM; for Hosted we have CMK options with restricted access.
[01:37] Karen Brooks: How real-time are the audit logs? We need near-real-time ingestion into Splunk for incident response.
[01:42] Jonas Chen: Logs are emitted in near-real-time; depending on the path (syslog, CloudWatch), ingestion latency is typically a few seconds to a minute. For pilot we can prove end-to-end by sending a few synthetic events and verifying ingestion.
[01:52] Lindsay Park: What about data residency and retention? Pilot data will be PHI-like, so we need to ensure retention policies and also certs for encrypt at rest and in transit.
[02:01] Maya Patel: We support region control for Private and Dedicated, and encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest. For customer-managed keys we support AWS KMS and HSM options. We'll include retention configuration and purge tooling in the checklist.
[02:12] Dr. Samir Patel: Great. Now on benchmarks: we expect to run a set of 100k tokens/day workload with 2-3 concurrent request patterns - chat/assistant queries with ~512 tokens. Success criteria: median latency under 300ms per token? Or per response? We need to agree what to measure.
[02:29] Jonas Chen: Typically we measure per-token latency at the runtime level and end-to-end response latency for user-observed metric. For a model with 512 token sequences, median E2E should be under X - depends on model choices. For pilot, we can benchmark both latency and throughput. Our recommended SLO for Dedicated with 8xA100 type capacity would be median response latency under 1s for 512-token completions when batched conservatively. But we should pick final success numbers together.
[02:54] Karen Brooks: Cost is also a gating factor. We need clear cost estimates for the pilot footprint and then for projected monthly ops.
[03:01] Maya Patel: We'll produce an estimated cost sheet based on your sample workload. Jonas will share a benchmarking spreadsheet where you can plug in token counts and concurrency to estimate throughput and cost.
[03:10] Lindsay Park: For the PII concerns, what's your recommendation for redaction? We can provide a redacted dataset but need to know what Redwood sees during pilot - is any raw data stored?
[03:20] Jonas Chen: For Private deployment, data stays in your VPC; we don't store customer prompts in our hosted logs unless configured. For Hosted, we have configurable retention policies; by default logs are ephemeral, but we can enable retention for debugging - this is controllable and we'll show the controls. We also support pre-ingest redaction hooks.
[03:38] Karen Brooks: Ok, so actionability: we need the SOC docs, and we need to run a security review with our infosec team. How long does that usually take?
[03:45] Maya Patel: Usually 5-10 business days for a first pass. If they have standard questions we'll answer quickly. For deeper infra/pen testing asks, add another couple of weeks. For the pilot, a 4-week window from kickoff is reasonable if the security review is completed beforehand.
[03:59] Dr. Samir Patel: Pilot length - we want 4 weeks to run benchmarks and integrate with our workflows. Acceptance criteria: 1) security sign-off, 2) throughput and latency within agreed SLOs, 3) quality measured via evaluation set (BLEU/F1 or domain-specific scoring) with less than 5% regression vs baseline.
[04:18] Maya Patel: That sounds good. We'll propose a formal success criteria doc. We'll need a sample eval set from you - a few hundred labeled prompts would be ideal.
[04:26] Karen Brooks: We will not share raw PHI. We'll provide redacted or synthetic examples that match distribution. Also we need to ensure logs forwarded to our SIEM don't contain PII.
[04:34] Jonas Chen: We can configure log filtering and field-level redaction before forwarding. We'll include that in the infra checklist.
[04:40] Lindsay Park: For SSO, we use Okta. We want Just-In-Time provisioning and SCIM if possible.
[04:46] Maya Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. JIT provisioning is supported via SAML attributes. We'll document attribute mappings and provide a sample IdP configuration.
[04:57] Dr. Samir Patel: On benchmarking methodology - can we get the scripts and a reproducible harness? We want to run them in our VPC to measure network impact too.
[05:05] Jonas Chen: Yes, we'll provide a test harness (python-based) that simulates user traffic at configured QPS and token lengths. It will output latency percentiles, token/sec, and cost estimates. We'll also include instructions to run it in an EC2 instance inside your VPC.
[05:18] Karen Brooks: If we run in our VPC, what network ports and peering config do you require?
[05:23] Jonas Chen: For Private via VPC peering, we need outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane for management (HTTPS), and specific SG rules we'll list. For strict air-gapped needs, we can discuss an on-prem bundle but that will extend timelines.
[05:36] Maya Patel: Let's walk through a proposed timeline: this week share SOC/ISO artifacts + benchmark scripts. Karen's team completes initial security review by Jan 14. Week of Jan 17 we schedule an SE deep dive to walk infra checklist. Pilot kickoff Jan 24, run 4 weeks through Feb 21, deliver evaluation report end of pilot. Does that align?
[05:55] Karen Brooks: Jan 14 maybe tight but we'll try. We might push kickoff to Jan 31 if security review drags.
[06:01] Dr. Samir Patel: We can target Jan 24 but are flexible. Also, who will be the Redwood POC for incident response during pilot?
[06:07] Maya Patel: Primary POC is me, with Jonas as technical backup. We'll also introduce a CSM if we go into Dedicated or longer engagement.
[06:15] Lindsay Park: On encryption: can you confirm TLS 1.2+ and support for enforcing our cipher suites?
[06:21] Jonas Chen: We support TLS 1.2/1.3 and for Private deployments we can align cipher policies with your security posture; we'll document the options.
[06:29] Karen Brooks: Pen testing - do you allow pen tests during pilot? We need to include Redwood in the test plan.
[06:35] Maya Patel: Yes, we allow coordinated pen tests; you submit a plan, there's a review, and we schedule blackout windows. For hosted endpoints there are constraints; for Private we have more flexibility.
[06:46] Dr. Samir Patel: Any required compliance add-ons or contracts we should be aware of for Private deployment?
[06:51] Maya Patel: For Private there is a platform fee and we include SOC 2 and ISO coverage; if you require custom contractual SLAs or enhanced audit data retention that's typically covered under an enterprise addendum. We'll flag that in paperwork.
[07:02] Karen Brooks: Good. On the evaluation metric side - quality threshold: we want at least parity with our internal baseline on intent classification and summarization tasks with less than 5% degradation, and latency within agreed SLOs.
[07:13] Jonas Chen: We'll instrument evaluation hooks and provide a dashboard snapshot from Redwood Console for token-level cost, latency, and per-route metrics.
[07:21] Lindsay Park: For the sample dataset, what's the recommended size?
[07:25] Maya Patel: For the pilot eval, 200-500 labeled examples per task gives meaningful signals; for load benchmarks, a few thousand synthetic queries to exercise throughput.
[07:34] Dr. Samir Patel: Ok that's actionable.
[07:36] Maya Patel: I'll recap next steps: send SOC 2/ISO artifacts; Jonas will share benchmark harness and infra checklist; Karen to supply redacted sample set; schedule SE deep dive week of 1/17. Anything else?
[07:48] Karen Brooks: Please also include a privacy/data flow diagram so our privacy team can sign off.
[07:53] Jonas Chen: We'll attach a data flow diagram and an audit log sample schema.
[07:58] Lindsay Park: Also would like a short write-up on key management options - CMK vs hosted keys.
[08:03] Maya Patel: We'll include KMS/HSM options.
[08:06] Karen Brooks: Thanks, that helps.
[08:08] Maya Patel: Great. Let's open for any quick technical clarifications before we wrap.
[08:12] Jonas Chen: One small note on model routing: for cost control we can route lower-sensitivity traffic to a smaller quantized model and keep sensitive traffic on a higher-quality variant. That helps balance cost and quality during the pilot.
[08:26] Dr. Samir Patel: Interesting - how does that routing work? Can it be attribute-based?
[08:30] Jonas Chen: Yes, routing policies can be request-attribute based - by route, header, or token - and we can set fallbacks if capacity is constrained. We'll show a policy example in the deep dive.
[08:41] Karen Brooks: We're concerned about silent quality regressions during rollouts - how do you handle evaluation and rollback?
[08:47] Maya Patel: Redwood Optimize can tie regression alerts to prompt sets/evals; in pilot we'll run canary rollouts with automatic rollback thresholds. We'll demo that in the SE deep dive.
[08:59] Lindsay Park: Sounds good. Anything else?
[09:01] Karen Brooks: No, that's it from me.
[09:03] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional misheard words (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cash"), speaker overlap, and some punctuation artifacts.
